fact_text: The UAE does not levy any personal income tax on individuals, so salaries earned in the UAE are not subject to income tax.
evidence_quote: The UAE does not levy income tax on individuals.

fact_text: The UAE's federal Corporate Tax does not tax an ordinary employee's salary: a natural person only falls within Corporate Tax scope if they conduct a business or business activity in the UAE whose total turnover exceeds AED 1 million within the calendar year.
evidence_quote: Total Turnover derived from Business or Business Activities exceeds AED 1 million within the calendar year

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the UAE's corporate tax means my salary is now taxed. Actually: Corporate Tax only reaches a natural person's business turnover above AED 1 million per year; the FTA lists wages, personal investment income and real-estate income as not being a business activity. Action required: no personal filing is needed for ordinary employment salary.

fact_text: Every UAE resident must apply for an Emirates ID card; it is the government-issued identity card and applying for it is mandatory for all residents.
evidence_quote: It is mandatory for all UAE citizens and residents to apply for an Emirates ID.

fact_text: An Emirates ID holder is legally required to carry the ID card at all times and produce it whenever required by law (cardholder duties under Federal Law No. 9 of 2006).
evidence_quote: carry the ID Card at all times and produce it whenever required by law

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: carrying your passport is enough. Actually: UAE law requires residents to carry the Emirates ID at all times and present it on demand. Action required: keep the Emirates ID on you, not just your passport.

fact_text: To obtain a UAE residence permit as a private-sector worker you must pass a medical examination approved by the relevant authorities; this is required for everyone aged 18 and over.
evidence_quote: A proper medical examination approved by the relevant authorities for those over 18 years of age.

fact_text: To be granted a UAE work/residence permit, a foreign national must be free of all forms of communicable diseases such as HIV and TB.
evidence_quote: In order to be able to obtain a work/residence permit, foreign nationals need to be free of all forms of communicable diseases such as HIV and TB.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the residence medical is a formality. Actually: it screens for communicable diseases (e.g. HIV, TB) and a positive result can mean the residence permit is refused. Action required: treat the medical as a pass/fail eligibility gate, not a formality.

fact_text: In Dubai, employers are required to provide health insurance coverage for their employees.
evidence_quote: In the emirate of Dubai, employers are required to provide health insurance coverage for their employees.

fact_text: From 1 January 2025, an employer must purchase a health insurance policy before it can apply to issue or renew the residency permit of private-sector employees and domestic workers.
evidence_quote: From 1 January 2025, employers are required to purchase health insurance policy as a prerequisite for applying for the issuance or renewal of residency permits of private sector employees and domestic workers.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: health insurance is optional or separate from your visa. Actually: since 1 Jan 2025 valid health insurance is a prerequisite for issuing/renewing the residence permit itself. Action required: ensure the employer's health cover is in place, or the residency cannot be issued/renewed.

fact_text: A residence permit for private-sector workers grants the right to reside in the UAE for two years, renewable for similar periods under the same conditions.
evidence_quote: A residence permit entitles private sector workers to the right to reside in the country for a period of two (2) years, renewable for a similar period or periods in accordance with the same conditions under which it was granted.

fact_text: Work permits are issued by MoHRE to the employing establishment (the sponsor); MoHRE has 13 types of work permits, issued depending on the nature of the job.
evidence_quote: MoHRE has 13 types of work permits. It issues the permits to establishments registered with them, depending on the nature of the job.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a worker holds their own work permit. Actually: the work permit is issued to the employing establishment/sponsor, tying your right to work to that specific employer. Action required: changing jobs requires a new or transferred work permit.

fact_text: The private-sector employment process runs in order: receive a formal job offer, sign the employment contract, receive the work permit, then receive the work (residence) visa.
evidence_quote: The employment process in the private sector involves receiving a formal job offer, signing the employment contract, receiving the work permit and then, receiving the work visa.

fact_text: The employer submits the signed job offer for initial work permit approval, which MoHRE reviews; this approval is what allows the worker to enter the UAE, so entry for work follows the MoHRE work permit approval.
evidence_quote: The signed job offer must be attached to the application for initial work permit approval, which is reviewed by MoHRE to ensure all required documents are complete. This approval allows the worker to enter the UAE.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you can arrive and start working, sorting paperwork later. Actually: MoHRE must approve the work permit first, and that approval is what allows entry for work. Action required: do not travel for work or start work before the MoHRE work permit approval is issued.

fact_text: The employment contract, based on the signed offer letter, must be submitted to MoHRE within 14 days of the employee's arrival in the UAE (or from the date of status change if the worker is already in the country).
evidence_quote: The employment contract should be based on the offer letter signed by both parties and must be submitted to MoHRE within 14 days of the employee's arrival in the UAE or from the date of the status change if the worker is already in the country.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the contract is purely a private agreement with the employer. Actually: it must be registered with MoHRE within 14 days of arrival/status change. Action required: make sure the employer files the MoHRE contract on time.

fact_text: A sponsored worker in the UAE may only work for their own sponsoring employer; working for anyone else is a violation.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you can freelance or take side jobs. Actually: your visa ties you to your sponsoring employer and you may not work for anyone else without proper authorization. Action required: do not take outside/side work on an employer-sponsored visa.

fact_text: A fine is imposed for every day you overstay illegally in the UAE; renew your visa/residency in time or leave within the grace period to avoid it.
evidence_quote: an fine will be imposed on you for every day you overstay illegally in the UAE

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a short overstay is harmless. Actually: fines accrue for every single day you overstay after your visa/residency expires or is cancelled. Action required: renew before expiry or leave within the grace period.
